title: Collapsed module rail entries expose an accessible name to assistive tech, not just an icon inside a visual Tooltip
description: In OverviewModuleRail.jsx's collapsed mode, each entry is a `<Flex as='button' type='button'>` wrapping only a ModuleIconBadge (an icon, no visible text) inside a Chakra `<Tooltip>`. Chakra's Tooltip shows its label visually and can wire aria-describedby to the trigger, but that is not equivalent to an accessible *name* (aria-label/visible text) on the button itself — a screen reader landing on the button with no aria-label would announce it as an unlabeled button rather than e.g. 'Audit'. The expanded-mode buttons don't have this gap since they render a real, associated Text label.
steps: Using a screen reader (or the browser accessibility tree inspector), tab to each collapsed rail entry and read its announced accessible name
expectedResult: Each collapsed rail entry announces a meaningful name (e.g. 'Audit', or 'Audit · <kpiLabel>: <value>') via aria-label or equivalent — not a generic 'button' with no name. File a defect if the accessible name is empty despite the visual Tooltip.
